Bounded idea units:
U-S-0001-05-SR-09 (68-69): The verbal explanation of the object structure was insufficient, leading to a request to review the code directly to understand its processing logic, prompting a screen share.
U-S-0070-C01-01 (70-72): An LLM can process a text chunk containing multiple objects/ideas simultaneously. It will identify and store all of them, so there is no need to worry about truncation causing data loss or to strictly feed it one object at a time.
U-S-0070-C01-02 (73-78): A distinction was made between two transcript processing strategies: a "top-down" approach where the LLM segments a large chunk of text, and a "bottom-up" approach where the LLM labels and merges smaller, pre-defined units. The discussion favored exploring a bottom-up method.
U-S-0070-C01-03 (79-80): Existing bottom-up methods have significant drawbacks: using fixed-size chunks (e.g., every 3 turns) can incorrectly merge multiple ideas, while processing sentence-by-sentence is computationally very expensive.
U-S-0070-C01-04 (80-82): A new "dynamic chunking" method was proposed as a compromise. This method would read a sentence and forecast how many subsequent turns are on the same topic, grouping them into a variable-length block for the LLM to process.
U-S-0070-C01-05 (83-89): The evaluation plan for the dynamic chunking method involves comparing it against fixed-chunk methods (both N-turn and turn-by-turn) to analyze the trade-offs.
U-S-0070-C01-06 (88-89): Key evaluation metrics will be the number of LLM requests (as a proxy for computational cost) and the quality of the generated output compared to other methods.
U-S-0070-C01-07 (90-91): A formal evaluation framework using precision and recall against a human-annotated set of important idea units was suggested to measure performance.
U-S-0070-C01-08 (91-92): The hypothesis is that the dynamic method will achieve high precision and high recall, capturing important ideas without including noise or losing information. This research could become a resource on efficient meeting information processing.
